name: Royal Oak
summary: A pub on Columbia Road with a bar downstairs and a dining room upstairs, where Time Out's 2023 review found Modern European cooking. Time Out also notes it appeared in the sitcom Goodnight Sweetheart.

music.notes: A monthly pub quiz upstairs on the last Wednesday of the month, listed on DesignMyNight.

crowd: Time Out (2023) says Fridays and Saturdays can get uncomfortably busy, and Sundays can be a crush because of the flower market outside.

evidence.quote: Downstairs in the good-looking pub, built around a handsome central bar
Upstairs At The Royal Oak

73 Columbia Road, London, London, E2 7RG
Existed from at least 1839. Address formerly 19 Barnet Street. This pub was re-built in its current form in 1923.
Built in 1923, probably by A E Sewell, with classic Truman, Hanbury and Buxton signage on the exterior.
One of the Inter-War pubs listed in August 2015.
Ex Truman's pub retaining many original features despite being opened up with a single central bar.
Originally there were partitions creating three rooms and an off-sales but all have now been removed.

story.opened: Standing as a pub since at least 1839; the present building dates from 1923.
story.then: CAMRA's pub entry says the Royal Oak was a Truman's brewery house and was listed as one of the inter-war pubs in August 2015. According to CAMRA, the 1923 layout of three rooms and an off-sales has since been opened up, leaving a single central bar.
story.now: The venue's own website describes a pub and restaurant serving food, pints and Sunday roasts. DesignMyNight lists a monthly pub quiz upstairs on the last Wednesday of the month from 7.30pm.
story.vibe: Time Out's 2023 review found the downstairs bar more boisterous, while the upstairs dining room was described as calm and almost sedate.
worth_knowing: CAMRA says the old wall panelling still shows the brewery's beer brands, lettered in gold.
According to PubWiki, the pub appeared in a Kray film and in the TV series Goodnight Sweetheart.
CAMRA notes a small walled garden with plants.
CAMRA says the upstairs room keeps a curved inter-war bar counter.
